stimulus.body: Ausgangslage: A translator renders a line where the speaker expects the listener to already know the fact. The particle must confirm shared knowledge rather than soften or suggest. In einer Arbeitsnotiz zu diesem Punkt heißt es: Vier Aussagen werden angeboten; nur eine wird durch den Text tatsächlich gestützt.

questions.stem: Der Hinweis dieses Items lautet «Contrast ja with other particles / ja signals shared knowledge. / A small word that confirms a shared assumption». Welche Antwort folgt daraus?
questions.explanation: Close reading of the note yields this rule: ja confirms a shared assumption and signals expected agreement. On that basis "ja, confirming the assumption" is the supported choice. Option A ("mal, softening a request") fails because it confuses confirmation with request softening; Option C ("doch, softening a demand") fails because it confuses confirmation with suggestion; Option D ("wohl, expressing probability") fails because it introduces an unrelated particle.

questions.subject: GERMAN
questions.topic: Two particles that concede a point in speech
questions.learningObjective: Apply zwar ... aber in a review

stimulus.body: Der folgende Auszug dient der Überprüfung des Verständnisses dieser Form. Von vier Antworten passt allein diejenige, die sich aus dem Text ergibt.

questions.stem: Der Auszug wird an «Apply zwar ... aber in a review / zwar ... aber concedes. / Two particles that concede a point in speech» geprüt. Welche Antwort bleibt bestehen?

options.misconception: uses a confirmation particle as opener
uses a request particle as opener

questions.explanation: The passage gives the controlling distinction: zwar opens a concession and aber introduces the contrast. On that basis "zwar ... aber, conceding then contrasting" is the supported choice. Option A ("ja ... aber, confirming then contrasting") fails because it uses a confirmation particle as opener; Option B ("doch ... aber, softening then contrasting") fails because it uses the wrong concessive opener; Option D ("mal ... aber, softening then contrasting") fails because it uses a request particle as opener.

questions.subject: GERMAN
questions.topic: Two modal verbs that mark different wishes
questions.learningObjective: Identify wollen as the will modal

stimulus.body: In einer Arbeitsnotiz zu diesem Punkt heißt es: Vier Aussagen werden angeboten; nur eine wird durch den Text tatsächlich gestützt.

questions.stem: Mit dem Hinweis «Identify wollen as the will modal / Firm intention is wollen. / Two modal verbs that mark different wishes»: welche Option wird vom Text wirklich gedeckt?

options.misconception: uses the liking modal for an intention

questions.explanation: wollen expresses a strong will or intention, so it fits a firm decision to act. mögen, dürfen, and müssen express liking, permission, and obligation instead.

questions.subject: GERMAN
questions.topic: A modal verb in the spoken past
questions.learningObjective: Contrast preterite and perfect for modals

stimulus.body: Der folgende Auszug dient der Überprüfung des Verständnisses dieser Form. Von vier Antworten passt allein diejenige, die sich aus dem Text ergibt.

questions.stem: Wendet man «Contrast preterite and perfect for modals / The double infinitive is heavy. / A modal verb in the spoken past» auf den Text an, welche Option ist begründet?

answer.exemplar: The perfect requires a double infinitive, which sounds heavy in speech. The preterite avoids this and is therefore preferred in spoken German, as in 'ich musste' versus 'ich habe müssen müssen'.

questions.explanation: The perfect with a double infinitive sounds heavy, so spoken German prefers the preterite. ich musste is more natural than ich habe müssen müssen.

questions.subject: GERMAN
questions.topic: The polite form of the modal of permission
questions.learningObjective: Contrast polite and direct permission

stimulus.body: Ausgangslage: A formal email grants a guest permission to use a facility. The writer must choose between a direct and a softened permission form. In einer Arbeitsnotiz zu diesem Punkt heißt es: Vier Aussagen werden angeboten; nur eine wird durch den Text tatsächlich gestützt.

questions.stem: Der Auszug wird an «Contrast polite and direct permission / Polite permission is dürfte. / The polite form of the modal of permission» geprüt. Welche Antwort bleibt bestehen?

options.misconception: uses the wrong modal's polite form

questions.explanation: dürfte is the polite subjunctive form of dürfen and softens the permission. darf is direct, könnte belongs to können, and müsste implies obligation.

questions.subject: GERMAN
questions.topic: A small word that softens a request
questions.learningObjective: Summarise the role of mal

stimulus.body: Ausgangslage: A translator must render a friendly request in a chatbot. The particle must soften the request rather than confirm or suggest. In einer Arbeitsnotiz zu diesem Punkt heißt es: Vier Aussagen werden angeboten; nur eine wird durch den Text tatsächlich gestützt.

questions.stem: Mit «Summarise the role of mal / mal makes it friendly. / A small word that softens a request» im Blick, welche Option entspricht dem Auszug?

options.misconception: confuses request softening with demand softening

questions.explanation: What settles the item is the relation stated in the passage: mal softens requests and makes them sound friendly. On that basis "mal, softening the request" is the supported choice. Option A ("ja, confirming an assumption") fails because it confuses softening with confirmation; Option B ("doch, softening a demand") fails because it confuses request softening with demand softening; Option D ("wohl, expressing probability") fails because it introduces an unrelated particle.
